question.question: At equal training compute, does the mean prediction of two independently initialized 20-pass K1 post-BN 100K models beat one 40-pass model on the 50000 development rows?
question.deficiency: Same-recipe ensembling gains 5.70 meV (N=2) and 7.68 meV (N=3) at 40 passes per member, but costs N times the training. No compute-matched comparison exists, so the value of ensembling per unit compute is unknown.
alternatives: A 20-pass schedule costs one model more than the ensemble gain, so the ensemble loses
The ensemble gain at 20 passes is larger than at 40 because short members are more diverse
Ensemble value is real only when each member is fully trained
question.positive_decision: POSITIVE: 2-member 20-pass ensemble MAE <= 137.535 meV (3 meV below the retained mean single 40-pass model, 140.535 meV). The equal-compute ensemble becomes a candidate for the owner; nothing is adopted.
question.negative_decision: NEGATIVE: ensemble MAE >= 139.663 meV (the best retained 40-pass single) or the mean 20-pass single exceeds 148.535 meV. Close the route with no retry, continuation, 500K, full training, distillation or adoption. Between the two bounds the result is INCONCLUSIVE.

profile.hardware: Tesla T4x2 FP32, one arm per device
profile.cheapest_falsifier: Mean 20-pass single MAE more than 8.0 meV above the retained mean 40-pass single (140.535 meV).
